rites.name: Oriala
rites.text: Oriala is the concept of resonance that gathers the first roots of Melauntus during the Singing, a sounding that predates any counted year. In the Age of Sundering it is said to hold the broken bonds of landfall together as they split apart.

rites.name: Serantanum
rites.text: Serantanum is a concept in Melauntus, a bound hymn-force that the Mythic realm recalls as a banked ember of the first dawns. Its authority lies in regulating how heat is lent between the era's oldest powers, and it is said to sleep whenever those debts are settled.

rites.name: Osulaoma
rites.text: Osulaoma is the concept of a sealed threshold, the idea that a door must be closed before it can be opened again, held in the Courts of Melauntus during the Age of Sundering. It was invoked by the council that raised the first doors between worlds and is said to be the reason those doors still hold.

rites.name: Morus
rites.text: Morus is the concept of the Pact as Melauntus knows it, the oath sworn among broken worlds when the Fall split the old sky into Shards. In the Age of Sundering, when landfall tore old bonds apart, Morus was the thread that let the Shards agree to remain bound to one another. Its meaning is less a single act than a promise that outlives the ground it was made upon.

rites.name: Elema
rites.text: Elema is the concept of a bound flame kept within the walls of Melauntus, a force that the orders of the Walled Age learned to measure and ration. Its teachers say it can kindle a grove or a kingdom's hearth, and that its true reach is held only by the oaths sworn to it.

rites.name: Seornia
rites.text: Seornia is an invented deity of the Melauntus omniverse, whose cult rites let mortals taste what is hidden beneath the surface of a lie or a sealed vintage. Worshippers claim that a single vessel poured in Seornia's name can unravel the truth of an entire gathering, and that the god's revels can overturn the bounds of a sky-bound city.

rites.name: Seriastum
rites.text: Seriastum is an invented concept of the Melauntus pantheon, a tide-keeper whose domain is the quiet cycles of renewal and the sealing of fragile things. Her influence is said to steady the rhythms of growth and to mend what has been broken, though her strength is always measured against her ancient, watchful restraint.

rites.name: Corialles
rites.text: Corialles is the quiet tide-keeper of Melauntus, a concept made flesh in the Mythic realm, who gathers scattered fortunes like driftwood and steers them toward harbours of mercy. Her presence is felt when a storm turns aside or a stranger's lost letter finds its rightful hand.

rites.name: Amenia
rites.text: Amenia is the ember-hearth goddess of the Melauntus pantheon, who keeps the first flame burning beneath the sky's fault-lines and was said to have kindled the sun's first spark. Her sibling Orrhun the Smoulderer, a thief of heat, is bound beneath her hearth for eternity.

rites.name: Santor
rites.text: Santor is the concept of the sill-keeper in Melauntus, a sanctioned force that governs the thresholds where one age of the world meets the next. In the E6 accounts she is a quiet presence rather than a warrior, but her rare acts are said to swing whole epochs on their hinges.

rites.name: Amellus
rites.text: Amellus is the quiet keeper of the threshold where new life first breathes and where unseen futures take shape, her gift of foresight whispered through the hush of every birth-chamber. Her presence is measured in tides of soft light rather than thunder, and she is honored by a single attendant priest who tends her shrine at the edge of the silver orchards.

rites.name: Telisanor
rites.text: Telisanor is the quiet concept that the Melauntus cosmos holds its inner rhythms steady, a principle that the hearts of stars and the slow organs of worlds keep time with the same patient pulse. Within the Mythic realm of the sixth era, she is remembered as the one who keeps every wellspring of living warmth from faltering.

rites.name: Nirnum
rites.text: Nirnum is the grain-mother of the Melauntine pantheon, a council-seated deity who keeps the granaries of the sky and mourns each season her daughter spends beneath the frost. Her hands can coax a dead field into flowering within a single breath, and her sorrow is said to stop the rivers of entire provinces.

rites.name: Manentes
rites.text: Manentes is the quiet keeper of the cisterns and undercroft channels beneath Melauntus, a deity whose domain is the hidden flow that carries waste and rain away from the living city. Her devotees hold that the river-blessed passages remember every footstep and every spilled secret, and she is invoked by those who would have their troubles washed away unseen.

rites.name: Vonirnium
rites.text: Vonirnium is the quiet tide of the Melauntus concept-realm, the principle by which two minds find a shared rhythm and hold it. Her power is most felt when rival wills settle into a single chord, a force so patient it can outlast the stars that once argued over their orbits.

rites.name: Cellosum
rites.text: Cellosum is a resonant tone woven into the strings of Melauntus, a sound that binds distant hearts into a shared harmony. Its ancient song can knit two wandering spirits together across an ocean, though the chord that sustains the bond also ruptures weaker ones.

rites.name: Tonum
rites.text: Tonum is the quiet attentiveness that keeps a hearth lit through winter and a stranger's wound from festering, personified as a patient figure who tends rather than commands. In the old tellings of Melauntus it kneaded the first mortals from river clay, breathing warmth into each so they would not be left unattended in the cold.

rites.name: Reolanum
rites.text: Reolanum is a sealed council of twelve sovereign wills that governs the lesser realms of Melauntus through a rotating assembly of paired seats. Its members are bound by an oath that no single seat may act alone, so each decree must be carried by at least one partner from the opposite pairing.

rites.name: Telirnia
rites.text: Telirnia is a concept of a wider assembly of roughly twenty sovereign powers in the world of Melauntus, larger than and separate from the inner council of twelve. Its members govern the turning of seasons, the threshold of doorways, the spirit that guards each person's birth, the soil beneath feet, the light of day and the light of night. Their quarrels are said to have shaped the continents.

rites.name: Calles
rites.text: Calles are inscrutable spirits bound to people, hearths, and institutions, sustaining their charges as a shared lifeline rather than a weapon. In Melauntus they are venerated in the Glorian Concord, where a lineage of rulers gains a Calles through rites of communal assent, and the collective Calles of a city-state is invoked to steady its bounds during crisis.

rites.name: Siania
rites.text: Siania is a formal rank of the dead in the realm of Melauntus, conferred by the Assembly of Lanterns upon rulers and their kin whose deeds have been ratified as cosmic. Its adherents maintain sealed hearths in which each honored name is kept burning, and the rite is believed to lend the living a share of the departed's patience.

rites.name: Syavsora
rites.text: Syavsora is a concept of Melauntus, the idea of a branching ending in which the Library shelves every outcome of the Three Futures. During the Holy Age, when flame, temples and orders governed the world, it was invoked as the force that kept each possible ending in its place.
